About the project

Freenet is a decentralised network: there is no central server, and every node both uses the network and carries other people\'s traffic. This app packs a real Freenet node into an Android app, so a phone becomes one of those nodes, with no PC needed.

What it does:

  • Starts and stops the node as a foreground service, and shows how many peers it is connected to.
  • Opens the node\'s web interface inside the app, so Freenet apps and pages work on the phone.
  • Builds and publishes a website from the phone, with an HTML, CSS and JavaScript editor, or by importing a folder.
  • Keeps the site files and their keys encrypted on the phone.
  • Joins the Room chat, asking for an invite by itself.
  • Can serve the node to a PC, over USB or over the local network.
  • Checks GitHub for new versions and verifies what it downloads before installing.

Telemetry and the node\'s own automatic updates are turned off. The web interface can only be reached from this phone, unless you turn on host mode in the settings.

What this version brings and what is still to be done.

In this version:

• Keys made here work between the people who use the app: copy your public key, add theirs, and a check says whose certificate it is.
• Generating a key is immediate and keeps the same identity.
• A website can be cloned from a zip file and published.
• "Use with Tor" checks that Orbot is running.
• "Install the keys on the PC" shows Freenet's commands.
• The start button changes colour, and host mode shows a copyable address.

Still to be done:

• A password for host mode: the node has none, so for now host mode only belongs on a network you trust.
• No SSH into the phone: an app cannot give a shell to the system.
• The node itself cannot go through Tor: it speaks UDP, which Tor does not carry.
• Nothing is verified on a phone yet: every version is built and checked, not used on a device.

Install the keys on the PC
The commands to install Freenet\'s ghostkey tool on a computer and check a certificate.

The phone already carries the tool. On a computer, Freenet's own steps are:

%1$s
The first command installs Rust, the second the tool, the third checks it runs. The last one verifies a certificate downloaded from freenet.org/ghostkey: a valid one answers "Ghost certificate verified".
Makes keys on this phone: they work between the people who use this app.

The keys are made on this phone and work between the people who use this app: each one adds the other\'s public key, and from then on those keys are recognised. Freenet itself accepts only a Ghost Key it has signed after a donation, at freenet.org/ghostkey.
